newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh sows 14.5 mln ha spring grain vs 16.1 mln.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh sows 14.5 mln ha spring grain vs 16.1 mln.

text.p: Kazakhstan has completed spring sowing, with 14.5 million hectares planted to grains, a senior minister in the former Soviet republic said on Thursday.
"We have sown 14.5 million hectares to grains, including 12 million hectares of wheat," Zhanybek Karibzhanov, deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture, told a news conference.
Kazakh farmers devoted 16.1 million ha to grain last year.
Karibzhanov declined to forecast what the 1997 harvest might total. Kazakhstan harvested a meagre, drought-hit 11.6 million tonnes of grain clean weight last year.
He said yields on 800,000 hectares of winter wheat currently averaged 1.1-1.2 tonnes per hectare.
"The early spring with heavy rains was good," Karibzhanov said. "This should make for better yields."

Spring sowing was threatened earlier this year by a lack of cash to buy fuel, with both state and privately owned oil companies in the resource-rich republic unwilling to accept grain-based futures contracts.
"Farms received fuel on futures contracts," Karibzhanov said.
He said the government also provided 150,000 tonnes of seed from state reserves, mostly to Kazakhstan's western regions where drought saw crops fail.
Kazakhstan, five times the size of France and with a population of 16.9 million, is forging ahead with market economic reforms.
But the transition has passed by the country's northern grain belt, where nominal land privatisation has achieved little in dragging collective and state farms out of the Soviet era.
"This year has seen deep rooted reform in the countryside," Karibzhanov said. But he added, "The new private owners do not have enough experience yet."
